title: tests(identity): pin the unpinned admin-lifecycle clauses of identity-auth.admin-lifecycle-operations — coverage gaps from QA run #9401
body:
QA-source: #9401 · identity-auth.admin-lifecycle-operations · C0–C7, C9

The Tier-1 pinned sweep (#9401) found this item's pin (`admin-identity-audit-trail`, 3/3 green) covers exactly one clause (C8, audit-log shapes). Security-priority per the maintainer's 2026-08-18 approval of the QA landing plan.

## Unpinned clauses to cover with real tests

From the run record's gap list: ban persistence/reversal · password rotation · explicit-password-wins · set-role flipping gate outcomes · revoke-user-sessions mid-flight · owner_id FK clear on user removal · impersonation attribution + console visibility · **non-admin refusal of every `/admin/` route** (both sides, server-asserted).

The last clause is the highest-value single test: a route-walking probe that asserts every admin surface refuses a non-admin principal is exactly the shape that catches a silently unguarded new route.

Acceptance: tests land in the package owning the admin surface (likely `plugin-auth` or `packages/qa/dogfood` — triage to confirm lane); the item's `automated.ref` is extended so the next Tier-1 run scores it honestly.

---

## Status after PR #9664 (2026-08-18)

PR #9664 landed as **`Part of`, not `Fixes`** — it pins C1, C2 and C9's refusal half, and re-scopes the item's `automated.ref` honestly. It deliberately does **not** close this card.

| clause | state |
|---|---|
| C1, C2, C9 (refusal half) | ✅ pinned by #9664 |
| C8 | ✅ already pinned |
| C7 — console impersonation indicator | manual by construction (screenshot oracle) |
| C0, C3, C4, C5, C6, C9's allowed half | ✅ pinned by PR #11899 — see below |

## Unblocked 2026-08-24 — and the `Blocked-by:` line is removed, not satisfied

The `Blocked-by: #9652` line that stood here is **deleted**. What this card actually waited on was the *decision* about which `/admin/` routes admit a platform admin, and that decision is settled: **#9968** ruled B (2026-08-20, reaffirmed 08-22 — the `sys_user.set_user_role` action retired via PR #11530, the vendor route left mounted and vendor-gated) and **#9969** closed `not_planned` (the seven consumer-less routes stay 403 by design, re-implement-on-demand).

⚠️ **#9652 itself is still OPEN** — measured directly, twice, not inferred: `state: open`, `state_reason: null`, labels `[domain:services, pm:blocked, pm:blocking]`. Its remaining content is the vendor-predicate fix (its options 1/2/3), which is `domain:services` work and was never this card's dependency.

⇒ Leaving `Blocked-by: #9652` would have pointed the unlock scan and the half-state sweep at an open card and let them legitimately re-park a card whose work is done and whose PR is open. Removing the line is the honest repair; ⛔ pointing it at the two closed sub-issues instead would fire the unlock scan for no reason.

**Correction owed, on the record.** This seat's claim comment (`5401835392`) stated that "#9652 closed completed today". That was **wrong**, and it was wrong because I repeated it from the skills seat's release comment (`5396675454`) instead of reading the card. Taking another seat's assertion as a reading is the same error this lane made earlier today with an actor field, and the same rule applies: **when a claim decides what you do next, read the primary source.** The dev on this card did read it — twice, through two different APIs — and reported the disagreement rather than proceeding quietly around it.

The decision content that comment conveyed was nonetheless accurate and is what made this card dispatchable; only the coordination card's state was misreported.
